div.div:
1 نَجَحَتِ الحَاجَةُ , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
نَجَحَ ; and ↓ انجحت , (Msb, K,) inf. n. إِنْجَاحٌ; (Msb;) The want, or thing wanted, became attained, or accomplished. (S, Msb, K.) ―
-b2- نَجَحَ, aor.
نَجَحَ ; (Msb;) and ↓ انجح , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. إِنْجَاحٌ; (Msb;) He succeeded; he attained, or accomplished, his want, or wants, or the thing, or things, that he wanted. (S, Msb, K.) ―
-b3- [You say,] ↓ مَا أَفْلَحَ فُلَانٌ وَلَا أَنْجَحَ Such a one did not prosper, or succeed, nor attain, or accomplish, his want, or wants. (S.) ―
-b4- نَجَحَ أَمْرُهُ His affair became easy. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
